_policy: STATIC, HUMAN-REVIEWED DATASET. This file is NEVER generated by a language model, and no code path in this application is permitted to write to it. Overdose Good Samaritan immunity varies substantially between states and the statutes are amended frequently. A hallucinated legal protection is the single worst failure mode this product could have: it could persuade someone that calling for help is safe when it is not, or persuade them it is unsafe when protection exists. Summaries here are deliberately conservative and every record carries verified:false until a human has read the current statute.
_verification_required: Before any scored submission or public demo, a human must open the cited source for each state used, confirm the statute is current, correct the summary, and set verified:true with the date.
_universal_guidance: In every jurisdiction, calling emergency services is the right thing to do. Nothing in this dataset is legal advice.

states.summary: Kentucky has an overdose Good Samaritan law. In general terms, someone who in good faith seeks medical help for a suspected drug overdose, and who stays with the person until help arrives, has protection from prosecution for certain drug possession offences based on evidence obtained as a result of that call.
states.does_not_cover: Protection is generally limited to specified possession-type offences. It does not cover trafficking or distribution charges, outstanding warrants, or offences unrelated to the overdose. Whether parole or probation violations are covered must be confirmed against the current statute.
states.plain_language_line: In Kentucky, calling 911 for an overdose protects you. Call, and stay with them.
states.source_note: Confirm against KRS 218A.133 as currently enacted before relying on this in a demo.

states.summary: California has an overdose Good Samaritan provision. In general terms, a person who in good faith seeks emergency medical assistance for someone experiencing a drug-related overdose has protection from arrest or prosecution for certain possession offences discovered as a result of seeking that help.
states.does_not_cover: Does not extend to sale, distribution, or trafficking offences, and does not clear unrelated warrants.
states.plain_language_line: In California, calling 911 for an overdose protects you. Call, and stay with them.
states.source_note: Confirm against California Health and Safety Code 11376.5 as currently enacted.

states.summary: New York has an overdose Good Samaritan law. In general terms, a person who in good faith seeks health care for someone experiencing a drug or alcohol overdose has protection from charges for certain controlled substance possession offences arising from that incident.
states.does_not_cover: Does not cover sale of a controlled substance above specified thresholds, and does not resolve unrelated charges or warrants.
states.plain_language_line: In New York, calling 911 for an overdose protects you. Call, and stay with them.
states.source_note: Confirm against NY Penal Law 220.78 as currently enacted.

states.summary: Texas has a limited overdose Good Samaritan defence. Its conditions are narrower than in many other states and it carries specific eligibility restrictions, so the protection should not be described to a user as broad.
states.does_not_cover: Eligibility restrictions apply, including limits related to prior offences and to who may claim the defence. This must be read carefully before it is summarised to anyone.
states.plain_language_line: In Texas, there is some legal protection for calling 911 during an overdose, and calling is still the right thing to do.
states.source_note: Texas protection is materially narrower than most states. Confirm the current text before demonstrating this record.

states.summary: Florida has an overdose Good Samaritan provision. In general terms, a person acting in good faith who seeks medical assistance for someone experiencing a drug-related overdose has protection from prosecution for certain possession offences arising from evidence obtained as a result.
states.does_not_cover: Does not extend to trafficking or distribution offences or to unrelated warrants.
states.plain_language_line: In Florida, calling 911 for an overdose protects you. Call, and stay with them.
states.source_note: Confirm against Florida Statutes 893.21 as currently enacted.

states.summary: Ohio has an overdose Good Samaritan law with conditions attached. In general terms it provides protection from prosecution for certain minor drug possession offences for a person who seeks medical assistance, subject to requirements that may include obtaining a referral for treatment and limits on how many times the protection can be claimed.
states.does_not_cover: Conditional protection with usage limits and follow-up requirements. Does not cover trafficking offences.
states.plain_language_line: In Ohio, calling 911 for an overdose gives you legal protection. Call, and stay with them.
states.source_note: Ohio attaches conditions that other states do not. Confirm against ORC 2925.11 before demonstrating.
